checks.claim: US1 closure: each E-limit L=(0,Mu) determines a unique real V in H^-1/2 supported in supp m_R, with symmetric pairing, and ||L||=||M||.
checks.reason: Zero columns pass to the norm limit, and the sup over (u,v) gives (3). M_n chi_R=V_n gives Cauchy convergence with a fixed-R constant. Support passes under test pairing. The bounded smooth multiplier on H^-1/2 gives Mu=Vu on tests, so V=M chi_R and V determines M by density. This also gives independence of the approximating sequence. Symmetry passes to (4).

checks.claim: The fixed-R chi_R reconstruction and F lift enter only the identification, not any uniform norm.
checks.reason: The lift difference bound (1+||chi_R||)||M_n-M_j|| is correct and places L_F in the old class mathcalV_R with L_F i=iL. No later constant in (5)-(11), (14)-(33) contains chi_R or ||L_F||. The E-part argument of S Section 5 uses only V, L_E and the pairing bound, so the identification does not depend on the size of the lift.

checks.claim: Complexification adds no norm cost, and the form is Hermitian on the complexified space.
checks.reason: Real and imaginary squared norms add, so the complexified M has the same norm. The symmetric pairing has diagonal v(u1,u1)+v(u2,u2), so the diagonal bound is unchanged. Conjugation invariance follows from form uniqueness, and the spectral functions are real.

checks.claim: Form inequalities (5)-(6), with A>=1 (indeed >=2), form domain H1, Teschl closedness and Theorem 2.14.
checks.reason: Recomputed. q_V+c b^2=z^2+(1+K^2)b^2-v, which gives the stated lower and upper bounds, and the upper bound is <=(5/2+3K^2/2)z^2<=3(1+K^2)z^2. The lower bound is >=2b^2 for K>=1. The shifted norm is equivalent to the complete H1 norm, so q_V is densely defined, Hermitian, semi-bounded and closed in the printed-80 sense. Theorem 2.14 and (3.53) apply. The AM-GM use fits the printed Mathlib guards with weights 1/2 and bases z^2,(Kb)^2.

checks.claim: The quarter-power step (7), the negative completion and condition number (8) use E constants only.
checks.reason: The resolvent variational identity and sqrt(x)=(1/pi)int t^-1/2 x/(x+t)dt were checked with t=xv^2. The pairs (B0,2A) and (A,L_K B0) are both >=1 and give 2^-1/4 and L_K^1/4. The dual norm is ||A^-1/4 v||, which yields L_K^-1/4||v||_-1/2<=||A^-1/4 v||<=2^1/4||v||_-1/2. Since L_K>=6, M_K^-1||z||E<=||z||E_A<=M_K||z||E. M_K^2=sqrt(3(1+K^2))<=2(1+K). No H2 or 3/4-domain claim is made.

checks.claim: beta is the spectrum bottom, -K^2<=beta<=0, lambda<=K, and every spectral h has h+c>=2.
checks.reason: For unit u, z>=1 gives z^2-1-Kz>=z^2/2-1-K^2/2>=-(1+K^2)/2>=-K^2. A dilated bump translated outside supp m_R has zero pairing and vanishing kinetic energy. (3.52)-(3.53) and the projection-valued measure give equality with the spectral infimum. Nonemptiness comes from a unit scalar measure. See minor note 1 on the unstated z>=1.

checks.claim: (9)-(10): the bound 8(1+K)^2(1+t)exp(lambda t) depends only on the E norm, with all cases h>0, h=0, h<0 and critical rate handled.
checks.reason: The matrix (9) is the correct conjugation by (h+c)^{+-1/4}. Entries: h>=0 gives |C|<=1, upper <=1+sqrt(c)t, lower <=1. h=0 gives sqrt(c)t and 0. beta<=h<0 gives |C|<=e^{lambda t}, upper <=sqrt(c)t e^{lambda t}, lower <=K e^{lambda t}. With sqrt(c)<=2K, each entry is <=2(1+K)(1+t)e^{lambda t}, the block norm is <=2 times that, and the conjugation cost is <=2(1+K). No division by lambda occurs and lambda=0 is admissible. The 7/6 row negative control confirms the (1+t) factor cannot be deleted.

checks.claim: The actual physical Young flow equals the spectral wave of q_V, by exact application of S Section 5 at fixed R, with shift independence.
checks.reason: L_F lies in the exact old class and is built from the same V, so the represented form is the same q_V. Theorem 2.14 uniqueness then gives the same H_V under either shift. C_t and S_t depend on H_V only, and agreement on dense spectral-cutoff data extends by boundedness. Compact L with strongly continuous S_E and adjoint gives norm-continuous conjugates and a Lipschitz primitive, so Young equals the ordinary Duhamel equation. No F norm is compressed.

checks.claim: (11) bottom continuity with constant K+2, and the square-root bound for lambda.
checks.reason: An eta-minimizer for W has q_W<=1 since beta(W)<=0. So z^2-Kz-2<=0 and z<=K+2. |q_V-q_W|<=d0||u||_{1/2}^2<=d0 z, and |sqrt x-sqrt y|<=sqrt|x-y|. Only ||M_V-M_W|| enters.

checks.claim: US2 typing and averaging: Bochner Lr(I;K(E)) fields in the closed actual class, true-cell averaging with own last length and empty-cell null convention, contraction, strong density, and scalar compact finite-net convergence (12).
checks.reason: K(E) is separable. T_R U is strongly measurable and values lie a.e. in the closed span, since smooth tests are dense and J_R is bounded. Jensen gives the contraction. Continuous fields on closed [0,1] are dense, with error bounded by the modulus at mesh<=delta B. The finite-net argument with ||A-I||<=2 is valid on the compact closure of C_t's unit ball. All this is scalar-time compactness only.

checks.claim: (13)-(14): the completed averaging identity on H_I and the uniform-R freezing bound, with no spatial compactness.
checks.reason: On finite tensors Bochner integration commutes with bounded J_R. Both sides are bounded on H_I by (1), the contraction, and U (15) applied to A_delta C_t, so density extends the identity. U (15) with A=(A_delta-I)C_t gives ||barW-W||<=M_0 M omega_delta, independent of R. r>=2 is met.

checks.reason: Pointwise (11) with K(s), K+2<=3+||W1||+||W2||, Cauchy-Schwarz on the unit interval, L1<=Lr, and Jensen together give sqrt(3+2Z)sqrt(M_0 M omega_delta). Rate is >=0, Rate<=1+C_mean||Phi||, and Rate is continuous on H_I.

checks.claim: (29)-(30), section 7: polynomial balls, order of limits, and deterministic suprema.
checks.reason: Exponents r(3+kappa)+s(nu-r)<0 by choice of s, and r(3+kappa)-sr<0 since r/(r-nu)>1. log(1+B^s)<=log2+s logB gives 7log2+(4s+3)logB. checks.reason: E1 requires only zero-start paths and ||H_m||<=Kres, on all cells including the short last one, with left multiplier S_E(ell_m). Bad cells use (19) with convexity and denominator>=1, so c_B=Ctheta B 2^(nu-1) is independent of Kres. Choosing C_Kres>=c_B absorbs the v^nu bad term. checks.reason: ||ordered||<=Aprod z with Aprod>=1 gives max(1,||ordered||)<=Aprod max(1,z). This is an inequality, not commutation or displacement multiplication. Fixed B,M, b_delta->0 leaves 2c_B D_M(Kres^-r+Kres^(nu-r)) for every Kres, which vanishes since r>nu. Combining with US3b via sums of suprema gives (33). b_delta is a bare deterministic hypothesis.
